claims.text: As-prepared MnNiSi-based alloys exhibit a sharp magnetostructural transition and a large magnetocaloric effect.
As-prepared MnNiSi-based alloys have limited mechanical strength and toughness.
Nb is a ductile and magnetically neutral or inert element suitable for grain-boundary decoration.
Surface coating with Nb followed by controlled annealing can produce localized Nb segregation at MnNiSi-alloy grain boundaries.
The proposed processing will form a nanometer-scale interfacial layer at the grain boundaries.
The dopant-enriched intergranular layer will be thin and coherent.
The dopant-enriched intergranular layer will reinforce grain-boundary cohesion.
Grain-boundary decoration with the ductile dopant will suppress intergranular crack formation.
Suppression of intergranular cracking will increase ductility and fracture toughness.
Confining the modification to grain boundaries will leave the bulk magnetostructural transition unchanged.
The treated material will have higher fracture toughness and ductility than the untreated baseline.
The treated material will retain a magnetocaloric effect comparable in magnitude to that of the untreated baseline.
Mechanical improvement without loss of magnetocaloric performance requires the dopant to remain confined to grain boundaries.
Diffusion of the dopant into the bulk may degrade the magnetocaloric effect.
Formation of secondary phases may degrade the magnetocaloric effect.
The mechanical enhancement should persist under cyclic magnetic fields at magnetic-refrigeration operating temperatures.
